questions.title: Which club will Mohamed Salah join first after leaving Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season?
questions.background: Mohamed Salah has announced that he will leave Liverpool at the end of the season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Salah or his new club, or reliable news reporting confirming a completed signing. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first club with which Salah signs a senior playing contract following his departure from Liverpool at the end of the 2025–26 season. Transfer speculation, negotiations, and trial appearances do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the club.

local_articles.title: Al-Hilal join list of 20 biggest-spending clubs in summer transfer window after addition of Summerville
local_articles.snippet: DUBAI: Al-Hilal have broken into the list of the top 20 highest-spending clubs in the world during the current summer transfer window, according to Saudi business daily Al-Eqtisadiah. The window only opened in Saudi Arabia three days ago, but Al-Hilal’s spending has already hit $79.2 million after the signing of Dutch international winger Crysencio Summerville following his performances at the World Cup. The Riyadh club paid English Championship side West Ham United $73.4 million for the 24-year-old, according to the latest updates on Transfermarkt, a platform which specializes in player transfers and their market value. Al-Hilal’s summer transfer activity now involves 11 players, with the total market value of $79.2 million. questions.background: Rodri is a midfielder for Manchester City.

Lifting Real Madrid from 0.48 -> 0.55 (capped at 0.55 since formal club-to-club talks have not yet begun, City still hope to keep him, and pending back surgery adds execution risk), trimming Atletico Madrid (0.15 -> 0.14), Barcelona (0.13 -> 0.11), PSG (0.10 -> 0.08), and Bayern Munich (0.04 -> 0.03), with 9% residual.

local_articles.title: Man City's Rodri sidelined for 'short period' following back surgery
local_articles.snippet: LONDON — Spain's World Cup-winning captain Rodri will be sidelined for a short period following minor back surgery, Manchester City said on Tuesday. local_articles.title: Man City's Rodri undergoes back surgery
local_articles.snippet: July 28 - Spain midfielder Rodri has undergone minor back surgery, his Premier League club Manchester City said on Tuesday. The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner, who was named the player of the tournament as he captained Spain to World Cup glory this month, had been experiencing discomfort in his back before finally opting for surgery. "The midfielder had been feeling discomfort for some time but has now undergone a procedure to address the issue and will now begin a short period of rehabilitation," City said in a statement. City did not give a timeline for his return but British media reported he may miss the start of the league season which kicks off on August 21. The 30-year-old Rodri, who has suffered serious knee injuries during his career, has one year left on his City contract and has been linked with a move to Real Madrid. REUTERS

questions.title: Which major US employment sector will shed the most jobs in July 2026?
questions.background: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reports monthly changes in nonfarm payroll employment by sector.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the broad employment sector with the largest net decline in payroll jobs in July 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' initial employment report for that month, released in August 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-07 Accepted Answer Format : Compare sectors by the number of jobs lost, not percentage changes, and count subsectors within their parent sectors. Answer with the sector's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Today's June 2026 BLS Employment Situation release (July 2) reshapes July sector-loss probabilities: nonfarm payrolls slowed sharply to +57,000 (with April revised down 31k to 148k and May down 43k to 129k), led by a massive -61,000 plunge in Leisure and hospitality—its largest drop since 2020 due to weaker-than-usual seasonal hiring despite the FIFA World Cup and amid immigration-driven labor supply constraints. Conversely, Professional and business services jumped +36,000, healthcare (+22k) and social assistance (+25k) grew briskly, and Financial activities (previously -11k Apr, -22k May), Manufacturing, Construction, and all Trade, transportation, and utilities subsectors were stagnant. Because resolution compares absolute jobs lost across broad parent supersectors, large high-variance sectors dominate: Leisure and hospitality enters as #1 (0.20, ~16.8M jobs, extreme summer seasonal-adjustment variance plus World Cup host cities winding down to 4 venues by the July 12-18 survey week, even allowing for partial mean reversion), alongside Trade, transportation, and utilities (0.16, ~29M combined jobs, stagnant across wholesale/retail/transport), Financial activities (0.16, down from 0.24 after stabilizing in June but still ~-100k YoY), Government (0.13, ~23.5M jobs with heavy July state/local education seasonal swings and federal restraint), and Professional and business services (0.12, down from 0.16 after +36k June jump, retaining variance/payback risk). Roughly 23% stays outside the top five (Manufacturing ~9%, Information ~6% given its small ~2.9M base, Construction ~5.5%, Other services ~2%).

questions.title: What sentence will Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa receive at trial in her drug-trafficking case?
questions.background: Sarah Khalifa was arrested in Egypt in April 2025 as part of a drug investigation.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The trial court’s announced judgment in the drug-trafficking prosecution stemming from Khalifa’s April 2025 arrest, as confirmed by official court information or reliable reporting from Al-Ahram. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the trial court announces its verdict and sentence. Later appellate decisions and judgments in unrelated cases do not count. Accepted Answer Format : Provide a short legal term identifying the principal penalty imposed, or the court’s disposition if no penalty is imposed. If multiple penalties are imposed, report the most severe.
questions.current_reasoning: Major procedural and legal update from July 8-9 Arabic court reporting (Al-Ahram, Masrawy, Al-Ain, Newsroom): on July 9, the New Cairo Criminal Court adjourned the trial of Sarah Khalifa and 27 co-defendants directly to August 4, 2026 WITHOUT referring the case papers to the Grand Mufti. Under Article 381(2) of Egypt's Code of Criminal Procedure, a criminal court cannot pronounce a death sentence without first referring the file to the Grand Mufti and adjourning weeks later for final sentencing—meaning a death sentence cannot legally be handed down on August 4. Substantively, two further disclosures weaken capital sentencing: (1) Masrawy's indictment summary confirms Khalifa is Defendant #4 (financier/coordinator, plus personal drug-use and unlicensed firearms charges), behind fugitive ringleaders #1 and #2; and (2) defense counsel invoked a Supreme Constitutional Court ruling invalidating scheduling decrees by the Head of the Egyptian Drug Authority. However, the 3-member forensic committee and forensic expert testified on July 8-9 that 2018-2019 Minister of Health decrees explicitly schedule narcotics 'analogues' and confirmed the lab analysis was technically sound, while the court firmly rejected defense procedural challenges. Accordingly, cutting Death penalty sharply 0.28 -> 0.06 (retaining 6% only if the court issues a Mufti referral on Aug 4 for a later verdict), lifting Life imprisonment 0.46 -> 0.56 as the primary statutory penalty under Narcotics Law Art. 33, raising Aggravated imprisonment 0.13 -> 0.19 (Art. 17 clemency or lesser trafficking/firearms counts), Acquittal 0.07 -> 0.11 (Constitutional Court scheduling defense), and Imprisonment 0.04 -> 0.06 (conviction only on drug use/minor counts), with 2% residual.

questions.title: Which month of 2026 will have the highest ICE arrest total in the data publicly available by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carries out arrests as part of federal immigration enforcement.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Use government data supplied by ICE, as reported by The Associated Press. Resolution Date : Resolve to the calendar month of 2026 with the largest arrest total among the months covered by the latest ICE monthly figures publicly available by August 26, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the month name only.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-20/22 breaking data release completely overturns the prior blackout thesis: on Monday July 20, ICE ended its 3+ month reporting hiatus (since April 9) and published official Detention Management statistics covering through July 11, 2026 (reported July 21-22 by CBS News, The Guardian, ABC News, Stateline, Denver Gazette, Deseret News, and EFE). Two decisive facts follow: (1) June 2026 logged 43,138 total arrests/detention book-ins (39,563 ICE + 3,575 CBP, averaging 1,438/day) — officially confirmed as the highest monthly total of Trump's second term, surpassing December 2025 (42,107) and every month January-May 2026, collapsing January from 0.54 to 0.04 (retained only for small edge-case risk that AP cites an alternate ICE-only DDP FOIA series still ending March 11); (2) July 1-11 surged even higher to 1,593 arrests/day (~17,523 total; 16,213 ICE-only), putting 31-day July on track for ~49,000-50,000 arrests (needing only ~1,281/day over July 12-31 to beat June, while Trump immediately reversed the brief July 15 vehicle-stop pause and DHS Sec Mullin boasted July 17 of hitting single-day records daily). Conditional on full-month July figures being published by August 26 (~70% likely given ICE just resumed publishing with a 9-day lag and has 37 days / ~2-3 biweekly cycles before Aug 26), July beats June ~89% of the time -> July 0.62. June rises to 0.32 to reflect ~25-30% risk that ICE slips into another reporting delay past Aug 26 (or only covers partial July) plus ~10% conditional chance of a late-July operational drop; August holds 0.01 (1% residual).
